What was the agricultural revolution in the Americas?
column2: Mesoamerican farmers domesticated squash and later beans and corn, which let people store food, settle permanently and build cities.

column1: Why did Native Americans lack immunity to European diseases?
column2: With few domesticated animals, Native Americans never caught the livestock diseases, such as smallpox, that Europeans had survived as children.

column1: What was the Columbian Exchange?
column2: The Columbian Exchange was the swap of crops, animals and diseases between the Americas and Europe and Africa that followed Columbus's voyages.

column1: Why did Hernán Cortés and the Spanish conquer the Aztecs so quickly?
column2: Hernán Cortés won with Indian allies who hated Aztec rule, smallpox epidemics, and Spanish guns, steel and horses.

column1: What did Martin Luther teach that split the Catholic Church?
column2: Martin Luther taught that people were saved by faith alone through God's grace, not by good works and sacraments.

column1: Why did Walter Raleigh's Roanoke colony fail?
column2: Roanoke failed because English leaders abused Wingina's people and the Spanish Armada crisis cut off the colony's supplies.

column1: Why did Powhatan let the Jamestown colonists survive?
column2: Powhatan let the English survive because their trade goods and weapons helped him strengthen his own power.

column1: What did John Rolfe give Virginia?
column2: John Rolfe introduced the tobacco crop that made Virginia profitable.

column1: What was the headright system?
column2: Virginia's headright system gave land to anyone who paid a laborer's passage, which drove the import of indentured servants.

column1: What did England's Navigation Acts do?
column2: Charles II's Navigation Acts forced colonial trade onto English ships and through England so the mother country profited.

column1: What caused Nathaniel Bacon's Rebellion in 1676?
column2: Falling tobacco prices, landless freed servants and Indian conflict turned frontier Virginians under Nathaniel Bacon against Governor Berkeley.

column1: What caused the 1680 Pueblo Revolt?
column2: Spanish forced labor, disease, famine and repression of Pueblo religion united the Pueblos to drive the Spanish out of New Mexico.

column1: What caused the 1715 Yamasee War?
column2: The Yamasees attacked South Carolina because they feared Carolina traders would enslave them next.

column1: What animal was at the center of the French fur trade?
column2: The beaver was at the center of the fur trade because Europeans prized beaver-felt hats.

column1: What was the main corridor of French expansion into North America?
column2: The St. Lawrence River valley was France's main corridor into the continent.

column1: Who did most of the actual work in the French fur trade?
column2: Indian trading partners such as the Hurons did most of the trapping and hauling, so the French needed few settlers.

column1: How did Separatists differ from other Puritans?
column2: Separatists such as the Plymouth Pilgrims wanted to leave the Church of England, while Congregationalist Puritans wanted to reform it from within.

column1: What did John Winthrop call Massachusetts Bay?
column2: John Winthrop called Massachusetts Bay a "city upon a hill," a godly model for the world to watch.

column1: How did New England migrants differ from Chesapeake migrants?
column2: New England migrants came in family groups, while Chesapeake migrants were mostly young single men.

column1: Which Puritan belief fueled their zeal to improve society?
column2: The Puritan belief in predestination, that an all-powerful God controlled history, fueled their zeal to reform society.

column1: Where did the 1692 witchcraft hysteria happen?
column2: The witchcraft hysteria happened in Salem, Massachusetts.

column1: How did New Netherland become New York?
column2: The Dutch had virtually abandoned New Netherland when an English fleet took it and renamed it New York.

column1: How did William Penn's Quakers differ from the Puritans?
column2: William Penn's Quakers believed the state should guarantee freedom of worship to all, and they dealt fairly with Indians.

column1: What was the Glorious Revolution of 1688?
column2: Parliament ousted the Stuart king James II and brought in William and Mary, who accepted Parliament's rule and ended the Dominion of New England.

column1: What were Spain's presidios and why did Spain settle Texas?
column2: Presidios were Spain's military outposts, and Spain settled Texas as a buffer against French encroachment.

column1: What did Indians call French Jesuit missionaries?
column2: Indians called the French Jesuit missionaries "Black Robes."

column1: Why did France stop importing slaves to Louisiana?
column2: France stopped importing slaves to Louisiana after the near-disastrous 1729 Natchez uprising.

column1: What was the Stono Rebellion?
column2: The 1739 Stono Rebellion in South Carolina was the largest slave rebellion in the British mainland colonies.

column1: What did the Great Awakening do to colonial churches?
column2: George Whitefield's Great Awakening revived a Calvinist call for a "new birth," split churches and grew the Presbyterians and Baptists.

column1: Who was the leading American Enlightenment figure?
column2: Benjamin Franklin was the leading American proponent of the Enlightenment's faith in human reason.

column1: What was "benign neglect"?
column2: Benign neglect was Britain's loose rule over its colonies, which let colonists govern themselves and made them proud to be English.

column1: What does "natural increase" mean?
column2: Natural increase means births outnumbered deaths, which was the main reason British colonial population grew.
